title: sparse-scratch-suballocator-and-kv-windowed-evict-policy
author: Aditi Rao
description:
Motivation: Large transformer workloads show high transient GPU workspace peaks caused by conservative scratch allocations (per-kernel worst-case sizing) and suboptimal KV cache eviction in bursty chat workloads. This PR introduces two complementary runtime optimizations: 1) a sparse scratch suballocator that subdivides and reclaims contiguous scratch segments at kernel invocation granularity to reduce peak workspace and fragmentation; 2) a windowed, workload-aware KV eviction policy that uses short-term access windows and hinting from the scheduler to evict cold KV shards proactively instead of waiting for global pressure.

Summary of changes (high-level):
- Add runtime/scratch/suballocator.{cc,h}: a sparse suballocator that maintains a small set of coalescing free-ranges and supports efficient allocate/free for per-kernel scratch with O(log n) search. The allocator is optimized for many small transient allocations and supports optional per-stream arenas.
- Modify runtime/kernel/launcher.cc to request suballocated scratch ranges instead of top-level arena slices for kernels marked as "scratch-friendly". A new kernel attribute (scratch_strategy) drives whether kernels get a contiguous slab or suballocated segments.
- Add runtime/kv/evict_windowed.{cc,h}: a sliding-window tracker that collects KV access timestamps per-shard and produces eviction scores combining recency and frequency within the window. Exposes a soft_hint API so the scheduler can mark shards as "prefetch" or "evict_candidate".
- Scheduler changes (runtime/scheduler/*.cc): integrate eviction hints with request routing so long-running chat sessions prefetch their own hot shard ranges, while background/ephemeral requests are tagged for aggressive evict. Also added a short-lived background defragmenter that coalesces adjacent free ranges in the suballocator.
- Add tests: unit tests for suballocator edge cases, KV window heuristics, and an e2e throughput/latency regression harness for continuous batching to ensure no tail-latency regressions.
- Benchmarks/telemetry changes: new smoke benchmark (benchmarks/peak-mem) and a Console metric emitted (redwood.metrics.runtime.scratch_peak_savings) to track impact over time.

Design notes and rationale:
- Suballocator strategy: previous arena strategies reserved per-kernel worst-case scratch which over-provisioned by up to 3-4x on common prompt lengths. The sparse suballocator keeps small allocations on a single stream and attempts to reuse recently freed ranges for temporally-local kernels (common in auto-batching). To avoid pathological fragmentation we: (a) prefer power-of-two bucket allocations with a small tail allocator for odd sizes; (b) run a light-weight defragmenter off the critical path that merges adjacent free ranges when utilization falls below thresholds; (c) allow kernels to opt into contiguous-slab allocations when they require contiguous physical workspace (legacy kernels remain supported).
- KV window eviction: LRU alone misses bursty access where items accessed frequently for a short time become cold but still pinned. The windowed policy computes an eviction_score = alpha * normalized_window_freq + beta * recency_penalty, tuned so ephemeral hotsets decay quickly. The scheduler emits hints derived from request attributes (session_id, priority) to bias eviction on background workloads and prefetch for active sessions. This tradeoff reduces peak memory by moving cold shards out before global pressure forces large-scale eviction.

Behavioral compatibility and safety:
- Default behavior is backwards-compatible: suballocator is enabled per-cluster via a runtime flag (--enable-sparse-scratch=false). New scratch_strategy defaults to CONTIGUOUS to preserve existing behavior until rollout. KV windowing is guarded by --kv-evict-window-size and defaults to 30s window with conservative alpha/beta so it only kicks in under sustained pressure.
- Race conditions: reviewers found a race when freeing ranges concurrently across streams; added a stream-aware lock-free free-list with epoch checks and falling back to a mutex path for pathological cases. We also added ASAN/TSAN runs to CI for the unit tests.

Performance results (benchmarks):
- Internal conversational workload (75th percentile prompt length): peak GPU scratch reduced 28-37% on average across A100/RTX-class runs, end-to-end token throughput improved 6-10% under sustained batching due to lower eviction churn.
- Tail latency (99th): unchanged within noise (+/- 3%), validated with 24h continuous batching harness.

CI and rollout notes:
- CI: all unit tests + regression harness passed in the merged run. One flaky e2e run failed due to infra GPU reclaim; rerun succeeded. CI checks: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), e2e-regressions (pass), lint (pass), safety-scan (pass).
- Rollout plan: feature rolled out to canary clusters with --enable-sparse-scratch=true and --kv-evict-window-size=30s. Monitor redwood.metrics.runtime.scratch_peak_savings and kv.evictions.count. If we observe >5% increased tail-latency for priority sessions, revert the kv hinting path only (flagged).

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the allocator free-list correctness across streams and the defragmenter heuristics (defrag heuristics are in runtime/scheduler/defrag_worker.cc).
- Kernel annotations: we added a small helper to mark kernels as scratch-friendly; review that the attention forward/backward patches use the helper correctly.

release_notes: Reduce transient GPU workspace and KV memory pressure by introducing a sparse scratch suballocator and a windowed, workload-aware KV eviction policy. Expected improvements: ~30% peak scratch reduction and 6-10% throughput gain under sustained batching for many transformer workloads. Flags available for controlled rollout: --enable-sparse-scratch, --kv-evict-window-size, --kv-evict-alpha, --kv-evict-beta.
